events.title: Bishops at the First Council of Nicaea adopt the Nicene Creed
events.description: The First Council of Nicaea, convened by the emperor Constantine I, adopted the original Nicene Creed, whose text ends with anathemas against Arian propositions. According to the traditional view, the creed was amended in 381 at Constantinople.

events.title: Louis IX orders Jews in France to wear a badge
events.description: An ordinance of Louis IX required Jews to wear a coloured circle of cloth, the rouelle, on their clothing. It enforced a rule of the Fourth Lateran Council of 1215 and marked Jews out for discrimination.

events.title: The Earl of Pembroke defeats Robert the Bruce at Methven
events.description: The army of Aymer de Valence, Earl of Pembroke, defeated Robert the Bruce's Scottish army at Methven during the Wars of Scottish Independence. Bruce, who had seized the throne that year, survived such early defeats and waged a guerrilla war.

events.title: An earthquake and landslides devastate Tongwei in Gansu
events.description: An earthquake of estimated magnitude 7.5 struck Tongwei County in Gansu Province, in the Qing Empire, and caused tremendous damage. Landslides triggered by the earthquake killed at least 73,000 people.

events.title: Moreau defeats the Austrians at the Battle of Höchstädt
events.description: Near Höchstädt on the north bank of the Danube, the French under General Jean Victor Marie Moreau defeated the Austrians under Baron Pál Kray. Kray was forced back into Ulm and later withdrew into Bavaria, opening the Danube route towards Vienna.

events.title: Hudson's Bay and North West Company men clash at Seven Oaks
events.description: In the Pemmican War, men of the Hudson's Bay Company and the North West Company fought a violent confrontation near modern-day Winnipeg, also called the Seven Oaks Massacre. The British government later forced the companies to merge.

events.title: Union troops proclaim emancipation in Galveston, Texas
events.description: General Gordon Granger announced that all enslaved people in Texas were free, two and a half years after the Emancipation Proclamation. The day is celebrated as Juneteenth, a US federal holiday since 2021.

events.title: Emperor Maximilian of Mexico is executed
events.description: Maximilian, the Austrian archduke installed by France as Emperor of Mexico, was shot by firing squad at Querétaro with two of his generals. Benito Juárez's republic was restored.

events.title: First Father's Day is held in Spokane
events.description: Sonora Smart Dodd organised the celebration to honour her father, a widower who raised six children. Father's Day became a permanent US national holiday in 1972.
events.html: Sonora Smart Dodd organised the celebration to honour her father, a widower who raised six children. Father's Day became a permanent US national holiday in 1972.

events.title: Julius and Ethel Rosenberg are executed
events.description: The couple were electrocuted at Sing Sing for passing atomic secrets to the Soviet Union. Ethel's role, in particular, remains disputed.

events.title: Kuwait gains independence from Britain
events.description: An exchange of notes ended the 1899 agreement that made Kuwait a British protectorate. Iraq claimed the new state, and invaded it in 1990.

song: the German labour movement; anti-fascist workers in exile
A marching song from 1934 by Bertolt Brecht and Hanns Eisler, asking all workers to join together against the Nazis.
